errors.english: two initiations such as the water initiation are granted
errors.why: The Tibetan gives two initiations at EACH of the north, south and east gates (2+2+2, plus the permission at the west = the seven initiations), not two in total.

fix.find: two initiations such as the water initiation are granted
fix.replace: two initiations each, beginning with the water initiation, are granted

errors.english: the initiation of permission (anujna) authorizing the student to practice a specific deity is given
errors.why: The Tibetan only says the permission initiation is given at the west gate; the explanation of its purpose is the translator's own (and does not fit the Kalacakra permission initiation).

fix.find: authorizing the student to practice a specific deity

errors.english: this refers to the purifications of the body and so forth
errors.why: The ablative ལས makes "other" mean other THAN the purifications of body etc., i.e. the purification of elements and aggregates; the English equates "the others" with the body purifications.

errors.english: the sun and moon alone perform the purification
errors.why: གཅིག་ཉིད is the unity/oneness of sun and moon (which the embrace of vajra and bell purifies), not "alone".

note: Readable and mostly accurate on the Kalacakra initiation sequence, but the distributive count of initiations is lost and an unwarranted explanation of the permission initiation is added.

errors.english: Therefore, it is said: "Because it is not something to be treated with reverence."
errors.why: "Therefore" (དེས་ན) is the lemma being glossed and the clause is the commentator's gloss; the English makes the gloss into the quoted root text.

errors.english: The phrase "other than that" refers to the concept of "identity in perception."
errors.why: The gloss says "other than that" means other than [the] oneness of the apprehension (ablative ལས), not that it refers to that oneness.

note: A competent rendering of a dense pramana commentary on recognition and momentariness; a few lemma/gloss boundaries are blurred.

errors.english: the appearance of the body is shown to be like the moon in water
errors.why: སྟོན is "autumn" (the moon in autumn water), not the verb "to show".

fix.find: the appearance of the body is shown to be like the moon in water
fix.replace: the appearance as a body is like the moon in autumn water

errors.why: ནམ་མཁའི་ཁམས is the space-element/expanse of space (akasadhatu), not the dharmadhatu.

errors.english: appears to oneself as an illusion within an illusion
errors.why: The Tibetan says one knows oneself that what is false appears as false, not an "illusion within an illusion".

note: Argument structure of the Mahamudra-siddhi passage is followed correctly, but two concrete term slips (autumn moon, expanse of space) need fixing.

errors.english: the complete transformation into primordial faith as it has been described
errors.why: ཡེ་ཤེས is wisdom/gnosis; there is no "faith" in the Tibetan.

fix.find: the complete transformation into primordial faith as it has been described
fix.replace: the complete transformation into the wisdom as it has been described

note: Accurate on the ultimate/relative bodhicitta and dharmakaya/sambhogakaya mapping apart from one clear term error.

errors.english: one should enjoy food, drink, and other resources to the best of one's ability
errors.why: ལྡན་པར་བྱ is causative: the master should provide (the disciples) with food, drink and so on as far as he can, not enjoy them himself.

note: A sound rendering of the feast and entry instructions of the mandala rite with one likely agent slip.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on the wheel-marked and well-planted feet among the major marks.
Faithful rendering of the erysipelas (me dbal) prescriptions; plant identifications are reasonable, though some remain conjectural as always for materia medica.

errors.english: the sound of a ḍamaru is heard uninterruptedly
errors.why: The commentary only glosses ghana as "uninterrupted" and kripita as the unstruck sound; there is no damaru in the Tibetan.

errors.english: With compassion means that the yogin does not make a cacophony
errors.why: The commentary glosses karuni as "the yogin" and ka-a-i as "does not do"; "with compassion" and "cacophony" are not in the Tibetan.

errors.english: Their bodies are "attired" with the subtle channels found in the different parts of the body.
errors.why: The Tibetan says that with it (the drops) one is to place/arrange [them] in the channels of the limbs of the body, not that the bodies are attired with channels.

errors.english: Śrāya refers to the absence of self in all phenomena.
errors.why: བདག་མེད་མ is the feminine Nairatmya (the goddess, selflessness of all phenomena), which the abstract "absence of self" loses.

note: The translation tracks the Apabhramsa glosses but appears to lean on an outside rendering of the song, adding and reshaping several glosses that the Tibetan commentary does not give.

errors.english: Likewise, because they appear in an unreal nature
errors.why: དེ་ཁོ་ན་བཞིན་དུ is "as it really is" (yathabhutam: knowing the body as it is, because it appears as something unreal), not "likewise".

note: A clear and accurate rendering of the commentary on the bodhisattva's applications of mindfulness.

errors.english: Having vowed that "I am a perfectly awakened Buddha,"
errors.why: དམ་བཅས (pratijna) here is to claim/declare, not to vow; the four fearlessnesses concern claims no one can rightly challenge.

note: Faithful to the formulaic four-fearlessness passage, including the block's own dittography and dropped negation at the end.
